compliance_decision:
**Compliance Answer:** The Reserve Bank may direct imposition of requirements on systemically important financial institutions when capital buffers are breached, including counter-cyclical measures and other prudential standards or regulator's directives.  

**Relevant Regulatory Basis:** Section 1(1)(a) & (h) [4106022-8act9of2017finansectorregulationa.pdf, Chunk 3397] of the Financial Sector Reform Act 2017

**Explanation:** When a systemically important financial institution breaches its capital buffer requirements as part of counter-cyclical measures or other prudential standards set forth by regulations prescribed under this section, it may face imposition of additional regulatory requirements. These could include directives from the Reserve Bank after consulting with the Prudential Authority to address solvency and capital concerns that arise due to such breaches.

**Human Review Required:** Yes
